content: Reporting a review finding with disposition "deferred" AUTO-FILES a storybloq issue. So for any out-of-scope finding, do exactly one of two things: (a) report it as "deferred" and let the guide file it, or (b) call storybloq_issue_create yourself with full metadata (location, relatedTickets, dedupeKey) and report the finding as "addressed" or "open" with a note naming the issue ID. Doing both creates a duplicate every time.
context:
Happened twice in the same T-008 autonomous session. First: ISS-034 duplicated ISS-033 (2026-07-31). Second: ISS-038 duplicated ISS-037 (2026-08-01), after I had already written the explanation of the first occurrence into ISS-034's resolution field. Both duplicates had to be closed by hand.

The recurrence is the point. Writing an accurate post-mortem into a resolution field changed nothing, because nothing about the next filing decision forced me to re-read it — the same shape as this ticket's dominant code defect (fixing a class in one place and not its siblings). A lesson is the structural version: it is loaded at session start, before the filing decision, rather than sitting in a closed issue nobody re-opens.

Prefer (b) when the issue needs locations or dedupeKey, which is most of the time; the auto-filed version carries only the description text.
title: Never both hand-file an issue and report the same finding as "deferred"
